items.title: Section: The Monastic Code, the Treatises, Hidden Intent, and Unobstructed Understanding — Closing the Basis of All Five Marks Entirely

items.zh: 於毘奈耶毀犯善巧、還淨善巧，當知是名第二依處。於摩怛理迦，施設、建立無倒法相，當知是名第三依處。能正顯除意趣難解諸法想義，當知是名第四依處。於一切法，法、義、釋詞、品類差別，當知是名第五依處。由此依處、由此所緣，菩薩能解甚深義理密意而轉。除此無有若過若增。
items.en:
Skill regarding transgression within the monastic code and skill regarding restoration to purity, one should understand, is the second basis.
Using language to establish, without distortion, the characteristics of phenomena within the treatises, one should understand, is the third basis.
Correctly disclosing and dispelling doubt about phenomena whose underlying intent is difficult to grasp, one should understand, is the fourth basis.
Commentary: Regarding "correctly disclosing and dispelling doubt about phenomena whose underlying intent is difficult to grasp" — every tathagata's own hidden intent and meaning is called phenomena whose underlying intent is difficult to grasp. Correctly disclosing this very meaning, and correctly dispelling whatever doubts arise for the beings being taught regarding it, is meant here. Its meaning is as explained in the Chapter on Genuine Reality.
Regarding all phenomena, their teaching, their meaning, their explanatory terms, and their varied classifications, one should understand, is the fifth basis.
It is by depending on these bases, by taking these as objects, that a bodhisattva's capacity to understand profound meaning and hidden intent turns and functions. Beyond these five, there is nothing to be added and nothing lacking.

items.title: Section: The Beneficial Fruit of Compassion — Breaking Resentment, Boundless Abiding, and Immunity Even From Poison and Weapons

items.zh: 菩薩哀愍，於諸有情，最初能斷怨害嫌恨。菩薩哀愍，普於一切利有情事皆能修作，心無怯劣。於此加行甞無厭倦，多住哀愍，能攝無罪現法樂住及饒益他。又如世尊所說修慈所得勝利，謂於現身毒藥、刀杖不加害等。如是一切菩薩哀愍，皆當了知。是名菩薩哀愍果利。
items.en:
A bodhisattva's compassion, towards sentient beings, most immediately breaks resentment, hostility, and hatred. A bodhisattva's compassion is able to undertake every task that benefits beings broadly, the mind never timid or weak. Applying this effort, a bodhisattva never grows weary, dwelling extensively in compassion, thereby including untainted present-life dwelling in ease, and genuinely benefiting others.
Furthermore, exactly as the world-honoured one taught regarding the excellent benefit gained from cultivating loving-kindness — namely, that in this very body, poison and blade cannot cause harm — one should understand that every kind of bodhisattva compassion yields this same benefit.
This is called the beneficial fruit of a bodhisattva's compassion.

items.title: Section: The Beneficial Fruit of Loving Speech — Breaking Four Verbal Faults Now, and Commanding Trust and Authority in Every Future Life

items.zh: 菩薩愛語，於現法中斷語四過。所謂妄語、離間、麁惡，及以綺語。由此愛語，於現法中能自攝受、能攝受他，安隱而轉。菩薩愛語，於當來世其言敦肅，言必信用。是名菩薩愛語果利。
items.en:
A bodhisattva's loving speech, in this very life, breaks the four verbal faults — namely, false speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, and frivolous speech.
Through this loving speech, in this very life, a bodhisattva is able to protect both self and other, dwelling in security and ease.
A bodhisattva's loving speech, in future lives, becomes speech that is dignified and composed, speech that will always be trusted and acted upon.
This is called the beneficial fruit of a bodhisattva's loving speech.
Commentary: Regarding "able to protect both self and other" and the like — not harming oneself, but gathering in and benefiting oneself, is called being able to protect oneself. Not harming another, but bringing benefit instead, is called being able to protect another. Not undergoing the bodily and mental distress produced by unwholesome karma is called dwelling in security and ease.

items.title: Section: The Beneficial Fruit of Valour — Freedom From Laziness Now, and Unwavering Resolve Towards Every Future Undertaking

items.zh: 菩薩勇猛，於現法中能離一切懶惰懈怠，心常歡喜；能受菩薩淨戒律儀，受已終無毀犯、退屈；能正堪忍，攝受自他。於當來世一切菩薩所起事業，稟性堅固，凡所造修若未成辦，終無懈退。是名菩薩勇猛果利。
items.en:
A bodhisattva's valour, in this very life, is able to leave behind every kind of laziness and idleness, the mind constantly joyful; is able to receive the bodhisattva's own pure precepts and, having received them, never violate them or retreat from them; and is able to genuinely endure with patience, gathering in benefit for both self and other.
In future lives, whatever undertaking a bodhisattva sets in motion, that bodhisattva's own disposition remains firm — whatever has been planned and cultivated, if not yet accomplished, will never be abandoned through laziness.
This is called the beneficial fruit of a bodhisattva's valour.

items.title: Section: The Beneficial Fruit of Giving and of Understanding, Treated Together by Cross-Reference — Closing the Beneficial Fruit of All Five Marks in Full

items.zh: 當知菩薩舒手惠施、能解甚深義理密意所得果利，如威力品惠施威力、般若威力差別應知。是名菩薩舒手惠施、能解甚深義理密意二種果利。是名菩薩五相果利。
items.en:
One should understand that the beneficial fruit a bodhisattva attains through open-handed giving and through understanding profound meaning and hidden intent should be understood exactly as the differing powers of giving and of wisdom explained in the Chapter on Power.
These are called the two beneficial fruits of a bodhisattva's open-handed giving and understanding of profound meaning and hidden intent.
These, then, are called the beneficial fruits of a bodhisattva's five true marks.

items.title: Section: The Sequence Opens — Compassion First to Gather Beings In, Then Loving Speech to Guide Them Towards the Good

items.zh: 云何五相如是次第？謂諸菩薩，先修哀愍攝受有情，於彼顧念，欲作饒益。次修愛語，為彼有情出不善處安立善處，宣說正理，攝受教誨。
items.en:
Why do the five marks unfold in this particular sequence? Bodhisattvas first cultivate compassion in order to gather beings in, attending to and caring for them, wishing to bring them benefit.
Next, bodhisattvas cultivate loving speech, so that those beings may be led out of unwholesome ground and established on wholesome ground, expounding correct principle to gather them in through instruction and guidance.

items.title: Section: Valour Comes Third to Sustain the Relationship Through Setbacks, Giving and Understanding Last to Match Each Being's Own Need — Closing the Sequence in Full

items.zh: 次修勇猛，於已趣入諸有情類，若諸有情起諸邪行，種種煩惱變異事中皆能堪忍，為不棄捨安住種種正行、邪行諸有情故。是諸菩薩修勇猛已，一類有情以財攝受，能令成熟；一類有情以法攝受，能令成熟；一類有情以財、以法二種攝受，能令成熟。是故菩薩次後修習舒手惠施、能解甚深義理密意。當知是名菩薩五相前後次第。
items.en:
Next, bodhisattvas cultivate valour, so that, towards beings already brought into the teaching, whenever such beings give rise to wrong conduct or undergo various afflictive changes, they are able to endure all of it, so as not to abandon beings who remain established in correct practice even when they also, at times, exhibit wrong conduct.
Commentary: Regarding "giving rise to wrong conduct" — this refers to violently violating the pure precepts. Such wrong conduct, one should understand, arises from various afflictive changes that alter a being's own originally wholesome disposition. Because of this, a bodhisattva generates deep compassion and is thereby able to endure it, in order not to abandon that being. Since such a being has already correctly entered the Buddha's noble teaching, this is called abiding in correct practice; yet at a given moment, deceived by affliction, that being temporarily gives rise to a violation, which is why it is also called wrong conduct.
Once bodhisattvas have cultivated valour, for one class of being, gathering in through material wealth is able to bring maturity; for one class of being, gathering in through the teaching is able to bring maturity; and for one class of being, gathering in through both wealth and teaching together is able to bring maturity. This is why bodhisattvas next cultivate open-handed giving and understanding profound meaning and hidden intent.
One should understand that this is called the bodhisattva's own sequence for the five marks, from first to last.

items.title: Section: Mutual Inclusion — Mapping All Five True Marks Onto the Six Perfections, Closing the Fifth and Final Angle

items.zh: 問：菩薩五相，六到彼岸，何到彼岸攝何等相？答：菩薩哀愍，當知靜慮到彼岸攝；菩薩愛語，尸羅、般若到彼岸攝；
items.en:
Question: Among the bodhisattva's five marks and the six perfections that carry one to the far shore, which perfection includes which mark? Answer: A bodhisattva's compassion, one should understand, is included within the perfection of meditative concentration.
Commentary: Regarding "a bodhisattva's compassion is included within the perfection of meditative concentration" — because the four immeasurables are called compassion, this is why it is said to be included within the perfection of meditative concentration.
A bodhisattva's loving speech is included within the perfections of moral discipline and of wisdom.
Commentary: Regarding "a bodhisattva's loving speech is included within the perfections of moral discipline and of wisdom" — based on comforting speech and congratulatory speech, it is said to be included within the perfection of moral discipline. Based on beneficial speech, it is said to be included within the perfection of wisdom.

items.title: Section: Valour, Giving, and Understanding Complete the Mapping — Chapter One Closes in Full, and Chapter Two Opens on the Householder and Renunciate Divisions

items.zh: 菩薩勇猛，進、忍、般若到彼岸攝；菩薩所有舒手惠施，當知即施到彼岸攝；菩薩所有能解甚深義理密意，靜慮、般若到彼岸攝。如是真實菩薩五相，當知一一皆有五轉。所謂自性、依處、果利、次第、相攝。已廣分別，應如實知。
items.en:
A bodhisattva's valour is included within the perfections of diligence, patience, and wisdom. A bodhisattva's open-handed giving, one should understand, is included within the perfection of giving. A bodhisattva's understanding of profound meaning and hidden intent is included within the perfections of meditative concentration and of wisdom.
One should understand that each of these true marks of a bodhisattva, in this way, has all five turnings — namely, intrinsic nature, basis, beneficial fruit, sequence, and mutual inclusion. Having now been extensively analysed, this should be genuinely understood.
Within the Basic Section, the Bodhisattva Stage, the second yoga foundation of sustained practice, chapter two: the divisions of householder and renunciate.

items.title: Section: Four Dharmas Let Both Householder and Renunciate Bodhisattvas Swiftly Attain Awakening

items.zh: 在家、出家二分菩薩，有幾種法正修學時，速證無上正等菩提？嗢拕南曰：二分諸菩薩，初事業善修、善巧、饒益他、迴向最為後。謂諸菩薩或在家分、或出家分差別轉時，略有四法，當知令此在家、出家二分菩薩正勤修學，速證無上正等菩提。何等為四？一者、善修事業，二者、方便善巧，三者、饒益於他，四者、無倒迴向。
items.en:
Through how many dharmas, correctly cultivated, do householder and renunciate bodhisattvas swiftly realise unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening? A summary verse states: "Bodhisattvas of both divisions; first, skilfully cultivating one's undertaking; skilful means, benefiting others; dedication placed last of all."
This means that bodhisattvas, whether functioning as a householder or as a renunciate, share, in brief, four dharmas. One should understand that these let both householder and renunciate bodhisattvas correctly and diligently train, swiftly realising unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening. What are these four? First, skilfully cultivating one's own undertaking; second, skilful means; third, benefiting others; fourth, undistorted dedication.

blocks.text: The five marks are finished: their benefits, their order, and how they map onto the six perfections. Then a short chapter on householder and renunciant bodhisattvas begins.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha made the precepts not to condemn beings but to lead them to purity and happiness; a breach is not beyond forgiveness, since it too lacks inherent nature. Venerable Miào Jìng: the treatise collection is the "mother of wisdom": mother means producing; it opens your wisdom.

Venerable Miào Jìng: the four immeasurables are not scattered thinking; they lie within the four form-realm absorptions. Master Cháng Bǎi: first it cuts off resentment, harm, contempt, and hatred towards beings.

Now it cuts false, divisive, harsh, and frivolous speech; in future lives one's words are dignified and trusted. Venerable Miào Jìng: your speech has power and purity; people believe you and act on it.
Venerable Miào Jìng: gathering in means guiding beings with compassion to cultivate wholesome roots; caring for them, one understands their circumstances.

"Some beings are matured by wealth, some by Dharma, some by both." Venerable Miào Jìng: some believe in the Dharma yet still do wrong; the bodhisattva accepts this and never says, "I won't save beings any more." Master Cháng Bǎi: those who love learning are gathered with prajñā.

Compassion is included in the perfection of meditative concentration: Venerable Miào Jìng, this is no ordinary compassion but the four immeasurables. "Valour is included in the perfections of diligence, patience, and wisdom." Master Cháng Bǎi: merit and wisdom are like a bird's two wings.

Skilfully cultivating one's undertaking, skilful means, benefiting others, and undistorted dedication. Venerable Miào Jìng: 持隨法, "sustaining according to the Dharma", means practising calm and insight according to it; having this capacity is "sustaining".

"Some believe yet still do wrong." Both teachers stress that the bodhisattva does not give up on such people. It is a good thought for anyone who teaches, or who has been disappointed by fellow practitioners.

quiz.q: The second basis — skill in transgression and restoration within the vinaya. How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the purpose of precepts?
options: not to condemn beings but to lead them to purity and happiness; a breach isn't unforgivable
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha made precepts not to condemn beings but to lead them to purity and happiness; a breach is not beyond forgiveness, since it too lacks inherent nature.

quiz.q: How do the lectures explain mātṛkā in the third basis?
options: both: the treatise collection, "mother of wisdom" — giving birth to wisdom, producing all meaning through repeated discussion
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: translated "mother of wisdom" — mother means producing; it opens your wisdom — the treatise collection. Master Cháng Bǎi: through repeated discussion it produces all meaning, so treatises are the mother of wisdom.

quiz.q: Compassion's fruit includes "untainted present ease." How do the lectures characterise this compassion?
options: Miào Jìng: the immeasurables aren't scattered thoughts but within the four absorptions; Cháng Bǎi: first it breaks resentment, harm, and hatred towards beings
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity aren't scattered thinking — they are within the four form-realm absorptions. Master Cháng Bǎi: first it cuts off resentment, harm, contempt, and hatred towards beings.

quiz.q: Loving speech's fruit: which four faults are cut now, and what happens in future lives?
options: false, divisive, harsh, frivolous speech; future words dignified and trusted
quiz.why: Now it cuts false, divisive, harsh, and frivolous speech; in future lives one's words are dignified and always trusted. Venerable Miào Jìng: your speech has power and purity, inspiring respect — people believe you and act on it.

quiz.q: In the sequence, compassion comes first "to gather beings in." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "gathering in"?
options: guiding beings to cultivate roots in the dharma; caring for them, one comes to understand them
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: gathering in means guiding beings to cultivate wholesome roots in the dharma with compassion; caring for them, one understands their circumstances.

quiz.q: After valour, why come giving and profound understanding?
options: some are matured through wealth, some through dharma, some through both
quiz.why: "Some beings are matured by wealth, some by dharma, some by both — therefore bodhisattvas next cultivate giving and profound understanding." Master Cháng Bǎi: those who love learning are gathered with prajñā.

quiz.q: Compassion is included in which perfection, and why?
options: meditative concentration; both: compassion here is the four immeasurables, entered as absorption with an undistracted mind
quiz.why: Included in the perfection of meditative concentration. Venerable Miào Jìng: this compassion isn't ordinary — it is the four immeasurables. Master Cháng Bǎi: cultivating them with an undistracted mind enters the samādhi of the four immeasurables.
"Valour is included in the perfections of diligence, patience, and wisdom." Master Cháng Bǎi: merit and wisdom are like a bird's two wings, carrying one swiftly to the far shore.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "持隨法" in "the second yoga foundation of sustained practice"?
options: practising calm and insight according to the dharma — having that capacity is "sustaining"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: 持隨法 means practising according to the dharma — practising calm and insight according to it; having this capacity is called "sustaining."

quiz.q: What four dharmas let householder and renunciate bodhisattvas swiftly awaken?
options: skilfully cultivating one's undertaking, skilful means, benefiting others, undistorted dedication
quiz.why: Skilfully cultivating one's undertaking, skilful means, benefiting others, and undistorted dedication.
